body: Confirmed S169-07's own precondition first -- 'write once it's actually resolved, not before' -- S169-01 landed the resolution this session (apps/lobby confirmed canonical via .github/workflows/release.yml's CI gate, apps2/lobby confirmed dead). Wrote the postmortem in the established SHANKPIT-460 first-person voice (matched against the two closest-precedent posts, 'I Don't Trust the Client' and 'Scoped to Prove Different Things', not invented fresh) -- the real story: two plausible client trees, the 3-button lobby menu (S170-02) built first against the wrong one, resolved not by vibes but by checking what CI's release pipeline actually gates on. Live-verified published: https://okemily.com/blog/the-lobby-that-was-never-going-to-ship/. Part (b) of S169-07 ('fragmentation as a witch', explicitly flagged as needing deeper voice care, not a rushed tie-in) intentionally left for a separate pass.
title: S169-07(a): client-tree-fragmentation blog post published
